newsitem.title: POLAND: Nomura sees Poland's 1997 GDP growth at 5.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nomura sees Poland's 1997 GDP growth at 5.3 pct.

text.p: Poland's economy is likely to grow by 5.3 percent in 1997 after an estimated 5.8 percent expansion last year, Nomura Economic Research said in its quarterly East European Review released on Monday.
It forecast Poland's trade deficit will grow to $12.8 billion from an estimated $8.1 billion in 1996, as imports were expected to grow 10 percent while imports 25 percent.
Nomura forecast the current account deficit would jump to $5.8 billion this year against $1.2 billion in 1996.
The widening current account gap will likely deplete Poland's reserves by $1.5 billion to $17.5 billion, Nomura said.
The report noted the central bank's concern for the fast growth of consumer credit and the tax cut inserted by parliament into the 1997 budget as potential inflationary impulses in 1997.
"We therefore believe that the government's end-of-year CPI target for 1997 to 13 percent is too optimistic and revise our forecast up to 15.5 percent," the report said. @

Nomura also said it expected nominal interest rates to fall only slightly in 1997, implying a rise in real interest rates as the National Bank of Poland pursues a tighter policy to curb credit growth.
